insights.title: External Score Combination as Primary Default Predictor
insights.description: Composite external score (mean of EXT_SOURCE_1, 2, 3) provides the strongest linear separation of default risk. Applicants scoring below 0.30 exhibit nearly 7x higher default risk than high scorers (>0.60).
insights.takeaway: Mandate high-risk credit review for applicants with composite external score < 0.35 regardless of self-reported income.

insights.title: High Debt-to-Income / Annuity Burden Escalates Default
insights.description: Applicants spending >20% of monthly income on loan annuities demonstrate elevated default rates. Critical burden (>35% DTI) shows the highest risk tier.
insights.takeaway: Establish annuity-to-income threshold checks at 25% to cap monthly payment obligations.

insights.title: Younger Applicants Present Higher Default Risk
insights.description: Applicants aged 18-30 default at ~11.5%, compared to ~5.5% for applicants aged 50+. Shorter financial history and career instability contribute to this gap.
insights.takeaway: Incorporate employment stability and guarantor requirements for younger applicants under 25.

insights.title: Historical Bureau Overdue Payments Elevate Risk
insights.description: Applicants with a history of credit bureau overdue payments show higher default risk on new loans than applicants with clean bureau records.
insights.takeaway: Perform mandatory manual underwriting whenever bureau credit overdue days exceed 30 days.

insights.title: Previous Loan Application Refusals Signal Future Default
insights.description: Applicants who were previously refused credit by Home Credit exhibit a default rate of ~12.0%, compared to ~7.5% for previously approved applicants.
insights.takeaway: Cross-reference prior application refusal reasons in automated underwriting rules.
